strikes.title: SANSAR Linux Cryptomining Malware Uses Modified NVIDIA Library to Hide GPU Activity
strikes.location: Linux systems of undisclosed victim organizations; exact ground-zero country not specified in the report.
strikes.data_affected: Linux system GPU and CPU resources; NVIDIA GPU activity metrics tampered via a modified NVIDIA library to hide unauthorized mining workloads.
strikes.impact: Linux-based systems of undisclosed victims were compromised and their GPU/CPU resources hijacked for cryptocurrency mining; the specific scale and number of affected organizations were not disclosed in the report.
strikes.prevention: Deploy file integrity monitoring and application allowlisting on Linux hosts to detect unauthorized modifications to system libraries such as NVIDIA drivers, preventing tampered libraries from masking malicious GPU activity.
strikes.summary: A financially motivated threat cluster tracked as REF3364 deployed a Linux-targeting cryptocurrency mining toolkit called SANSAR, a Rust-based orchestrator that communicates over the TOR network to manage CPU and GPU miners. The campaign tampers with NVIDIA GPU telemetry readings — via a modified library — to conceal high GPU workloads and evade detection.

strikes.title: Amazon Uncovers AI Agent Campaign Targeting LiteLLM, Dify, and Other Apps for API Keys
strikes.location: Internet-exposed AI application deployments globally, identified and tracked via Amazon threat intelligence decoy servers.
strikes.data_affected: AI provider API keys stored within internet-exposed AI applications (LiteLLM, One API, Dify, and similar platforms).
strikes.impact: Multiple internet-exposed AI applications were targeted across an indeterminate number of organizations globally; stolen API keys were actively weaponized to fund continued attack operations. Full scale of victim organizations and financial losses not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Restrict AI application API key storage by using secrets management vaults (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager) and enforce network-level controls to prevent unauthenticated internet exposure of AI management interfaces such as LiteLLM, One API, and Dify.
strikes.summary: Amazon's threat intelligence team captured AI agent-driven attack activity via decoy servers, revealing an automated campaign targeting internet-exposed AI applications — including LiteLLM, One API, and Dify — to harvest stored AI provider API keys. The stolen keys were then reused to power the AI models that fueled further reconnaissance and key-harvesting operations, creating a self-sustaining attack loop.

strikes.title: BO Team Exploits Log4Shell in VMware vCenter, Compromises Russian Firm's Code-Signing Server
strikes.location: Russian software development company — exact organization name not disclosed; network intrusion originated through VMware vCenter infrastructure within the victim's environment, Russia.
strikes.data_affected: Software development infrastructure, software code-signing server, and associated internal network systems of the victim organization.
strikes.impact: An unnamed Russian software developer suffered a prolonged, multi-month compromise of its core development and build pipeline, including its code-signing server — raising the risk of downstream supply-chain attacks via tampered or maliciously signed software artifacts. Full operational and customer-side fallout was not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Patch VMware vCenter and all Log4j-dependent components to remediate CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell); apply network segmentation to isolate code-signing infrastructure from internet-exposed services, and enforce strict allowlisting on signing servers to prevent unauthorized use.
strikes.summary: Threat actor BO Team (also known as Black Owl / Hoody Hyena) exploited the Log4Shell vulnerability in VMware vCenter to infiltrate the development infrastructure of an unnamed Russian software developer, achieving a months-long compromise that included access to a software code-signing server. The incident was investigated by Kaspersky's ICS CERT after the affected developer contacted them in June 2025.

strikes.title: Cursor Says Stolen Fireworks AI Key Led to Trojanized Claude Code Extension Incident
strikes.location: Cursor's extension marketplace (Cursor, Inc. — United States)
strikes.data_affected: Cursor-issued access key exposed via Fireworks AI breach; read-only data accessed via the stolen key; Anthropic's official Claude Code extension on Cursor's marketplace was trojanized.
strikes.impact: Users of the Cursor extension marketplace were exposed to a trojanized version of the official Claude Code extension; the full scope of downstream user impact was not disclosed in the report.
strikes.prevention: Implement short-lived, scoped API keys with automatic rotation and anomaly-based revocation so that any key exposed by a third-party vendor is invalidated before it can be weaponized to tamper with published software artifacts.
strikes.summary: An attacker stole an access key that Cursor had issued to Fireworks AI following a breach at Fireworks AI, then used it to copy data and trojanize Anthropic's official Claude Code extension on Cursor's extension marketplace. The compromise resulted in a malicious version of the extension being distributed to users of the Cursor platform.

strikes.title: Attackers Exploit UnrealIRCd Flaw That Enables Server-Level Command Injection
strikes.location: Organizations running UnrealIRCd open-source IRC servers; UnrealIRCd project is the vulnerable vendor (ground zero per vulnerable product HQ).
strikes.data_affected: UnrealIRCd IRC server instances; server-level command execution capability exposed.
strikes.impact: Organizations running UnrealIRCd servers are actively being targeted; full scope of affected victims not disclosed. CISA's KEV listing implies real-world exploitation across multiple targets warranting urgent remediation.
strikes.prevention: Apply the vendor-issued patch or upgrade UnrealIRCd to the fixed version immediately, as directed by CISA's KEV remediation guidance, to eliminate the command-injection vector.
strikes.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-114713, a high-severity improper neutralization of delimiters flaw in UnrealIRCd (an open-source IRC server), to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following confirmed active exploitation. The vulnerability carries a CVSS score of 8.6 and enables server-level command injection.

strikes.title: FBI Says North Korean Hackers Stole Over $400 Million in Crypto Using Deepfake Video Calls
strikes.location: United States — cryptocurrency holders and organizations targeted via deepfake video call social engineering
strikes.data_affected: Cryptocurrency holdings and associated wallet credentials of targeted individuals and organizations; exact systems not further disclosed in the report.
strikes.impact: More than $400 million in cryptocurrency stolen from victims across the 18-month campaign; U.S. government coordinated a formal response, suggesting broad financial and national-security-level impact.
strikes.prevention: Implement strict out-of-band identity verification protocols — such as requiring a shared secret or challenge-response over a separate, authenticated channel — before conducting any video calls involving cryptocurrency transactions or access credentials, to defeat deepfake impersonation.
strikes.summary: North Korean (DPRK) threat actors conducted a social engineering campaign dubbed FaceStealer, using deepfake video calls to steal over $400 million in cryptocurrency over the last 18 months. The FBI attributed the scheme to DPRK-linked hackers as part of a coordinated U.S. government response.

strikes.title: Trezor Confirms Hidden Implants in CryptoBilis-Sold Wallets That Can Steal Recovery Phrases
strikes.location: Trezor Safe 5 hardware wallets sold via CryptoBilis reseller channel; Trezor is headquartered in the Czech Republic
strikes.data_affected: Cryptocurrency wallet recovery phrases (seed phrases) stored and displayed on Trezor Safe 5 hardware wallets
strikes.impact: At least three Trezor Safe 5 wallets sold through the CryptoBilis reseller were compromised; affected users' recovery phrases — and therefore full control of their cryptocurrency holdings — were exposed to the attackers. The total number of victims and financial losses were not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Purchase hardware wallets exclusively from the manufacturer's official store or verified authorized resellers, and perform a firmware integrity check and physical tamper-seal inspection immediately upon receipt before first use.
strikes.summary: Three Trezor Safe 5 hardware wallets sold by reseller CryptoBilis were found to contain hidden implants — extra circuit boards capable of reading recovery phrases from the device screen and transmitting them over the mobile network to an attacker-controlled server. Trezor confirmed the discovery after examining one of the tampered wallets in its lab and identifying the remaining two.

strikes.title: SilentAir Hijacks Asian Telecom Networks to Intercept SMS 2FA Codes and Spy on Taiwanese Users
strikes.location: Mobile operator networks across at least six Asian countries, with primary targeting of users in Taiwan.
strikes.data_affected: SMS messages (including 2FA codes), voice calls, and associated subscriber communications intercepted via hacked equipment within Asian mobile operator networks.
strikes.impact: Targeted individuals in Taiwan — and potentially across multiple Asian countries — had their calls and texts covertly monitored; the breadth of compromise spans at least six Asian mobile operators, suggesting a persistent, wide-reaching surveillance operation against selected persons of interest.
strikes.prevention: Deploy SS7/Diameter signaling firewalls and anomaly-detection controls at telecom network boundaries to identify and block unauthorized interception attempts and rogue routing of subscriber traffic.
strikes.summary: A state-level threat actor tracked as SilentAir compromised equipment inside Asian mobile operators to intercept calls, SMS messages, and two-factor authentication codes, primarily targeting users in Taiwan. Cybersecurity firm Enea attributed the campaign with high confidence to a nation-state and identified attack infrastructure in at least six Asian countries.

strikes.title: Operation Endgame Takes Down Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC Servers, Seizes 6.4M Stolen Logins
strikes.location: International operation targeting malware server infrastructure; takedown coordinated by Germany's Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA) and international partners.
strikes.data_affected: Approximately 6.4 million stolen login credentials belonging to more than 40,000 victims; systems compromised via Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC malware.
strikes.impact: Over 40,000 victims across multiple countries had their credentials stolen via three malware tools used to gain system access, harvest passwords, and facilitate ransomware attacks; criminal server infrastructure was taken offline by the operation.
strikes.prevention: Deploy endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions capable of identifying loader and infostealer malware behavior — such as Gootloader's JavaScript-based execution chain — to block initial access before credentials can be exfiltrated.
strikes.summary: An international law enforcement operation (Operation Endgame) dismantled server infrastructure supporting the Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC malware families. Authorities seized approximately 6.4 million stolen login credentials linked to over 40,000 victims, with Germany's BKA leading the announcement.

strikes.title: Hackers Exploit PHP2Shell Flaws in Check Point Gateways to Deploy TSGA Backdoor and Wipe ESXi Files
strikes.location: Israeli organizations running Check Point Security Gateways
strikes.data_affected: Check Point Security Gateway systems running Gaia OS; ESXi virtual machine files (wiped); systems compromised via TSGA backdoor implant
strikes.impact: Multiple Israeli organizations were targeted; attackers gained initial access and elevated privileges on affected gateways, deployed a persistent backdoor (TSGA), and destructively wiped ESXi files. The scale of the broader follow-up activity was not fully disclosed at time of reporting.
strikes.prevention: Apply all available patches for Check Point Security Gateways immediately, specifically those addressing the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities and the Gaia OS local privilege escalation flaw, and enforce network segmentation to limit lateral movement from perimeter gateway devices to ESXi hypervisor infrastructure.
strikes.summary: An unknown threat actor exploited PHP2Shell vulnerabilities in unpatched Check Point Security Gateways, chained with a previously unreported local privilege escalation flaw in Gaia OS, to deploy a backdoor named TSGA and wipe ESXi files. The campaign began on October 30, 2026, and specifically targeted Israeli organizations, with indications of a broader follow-up operation.

strikes.title: Hackers Exploit N-central Flaws to Infect 21 Servers, Including 19 Running Hotfix 2
strikes.location: N-able N-central platform infrastructure (vendor headquartered in Canada); specific geographic location of compromised servers not disclosed
strikes.data_affected: N-central managed servers (21 total); server environments running N-central, including instances patched to Hotfix 2
strikes.impact: 21 servers infected across N-central deployments; N-able restricted platform features and integrations, affecting functionality for managed service provider (MSP) customers relying on N-central; full downstream customer impact not disclosed
strikes.prevention: Apply vendor-issued patches and mitigations immediately upon disclosure of critical RMM platform vulnerabilities, and enforce network-level access controls (e.g., allowlisting) to restrict exposure of N-central management interfaces to trusted IPs only
strikes.summary: Threat actors exploited two newly disclosed vulnerabilities in N-able's N-central remote monitoring and management platform, tracked as 4EverAble2Shell and Agent2Shell, compromising 21 servers — 19 of which were running Hotfix 2. In response, N-able announced it was restricting certain N-central features and integrations while remediation was completed.

strikes.title: 186 Fake AI Domains Redirect Users to ClickFix Lures, Browser Malware, and Search Hijackers
strikes.location: Global campaign targeting end users via 186 fake AI-tool lookalike domains; no single geographic ground zero disclosed.
strikes.data_affected: Browser settings, search engine configurations, and potentially credentials or browsing data harvested via hijacked browser extensions and ClickFix-style malware payloads.
strikes.impact: End users globally who mistype or are redirected to AI-tool lookalike domains are exposed to browser hijacking and search redirection malware; scale of confirmed victim infections not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Enable DNS filtering or a secure DNS resolver (e.g., threat-intelligence-backed DNS-over-HTTPS) to block known malicious lookalike domains before they resolve in the browser.
strikes.summary: Cybersecurity researchers uncovered a campaign dubbed "TypoPrompting" in which 186 lookalike domains impersonating popular AI tools redirect users to ClickFix-style social-engineering lures, browser-hijacking malware, and search-hijacking extensions. Victims attempting to reach legitimate AI applications are instead prompted to execute malicious actions or install rogue browser extensions.

strikes.title: SCKit Malware Turns ScreenConnect Support Sessions Into Potential MSP Attack Paths
strikes.location: ConnectWise ScreenConnect deployments operated by Managed Service Providers (MSPs); specific geographic ground zero not disclosed.
strikes.data_affected: ConnectWise ScreenConnect remote access sessions and downstream MSP-managed systems accessible via those sessions.
strikes.impact: MSPs and their downstream client organizations are at risk of full compromise through hijacked ScreenConnect support sessions; the scale of affected organizations is not disclosed, but the campaign is described as ongoing.
strikes.prevention: Apply the available patch for CVE-2026-84869 on all ConnectWise ScreenConnect deployments immediately, and enforce session-level authentication and IP allowlisting to restrict who can initiate or join remote support sessions.
strikes.summary: An ongoing campaign dubbed SCKit is actively exploiting CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS 9.9), a now-patched critical flaw in ConnectWise ScreenConnect, to hijack remote support sessions and use them as attack paths into Managed Service Provider (MSP) environments. Blackpoint Cyber's Adversary Pursuit Group recovered the attacker toolkit and shared details of the exploitation chain with The Hacker News.

strikes.title: Calendar Invites and Live Proxies: Inside a Google Session Hijacking Campaign
strikes.location: Corporate Google account users (platform ground zero: Google, headquartered in the United States).
strikes.data_affected: Live Google session tokens (authenticated user sessions) of corporate Google account holders.
strikes.impact: Corporate users across an undisclosed number of organizations had their active Google sessions stolen, granting attackers authenticated access without needing passwords. Hundreds of malicious domains were active before takedown; full victim count was not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Enforce hardware-bound, phishing-resistant MFA (e.g., FIDO2/passkeys) so that stolen session cookies cannot be replayed by an attacker, neutralizing session hijacking even when phishing links evade link-reputation checks.
strikes.summary: Since mid-August 2026, a phishing operation has been harvesting live Google session tokens from corporate users by using calendar invites and live proxies that bypass standard link-reputation defenses. Material Security's Threat Research team identified the campaign—dubbed Operation CloudFire—and coordinated the takedown of hundreds of attacker-controlled domains.

strikes.title: Attacker Used 4,837 Hijacked GitHub Accounts to Run a CI Secret Stealer in 1,806+ Repositories
strikes.location: GitHub platform (globally distributed repositories); ground zero is GitHub's US-hosted platform infrastructure.
strikes.data_affected: CI/CD pipeline secrets, cloud credentials, and repository environment variables accessible to GitHub Actions workflows across 1,806+ repositories.
strikes.impact: At least 1,806 GitHub repositories were compromised; secrets and cloud credentials reachable by their CI workflows were likely exfiltrated. The breadth of 4,837 hijacked accounts suggests widespread exposure across numerous organizations and individual developers.
strikes.prevention: Enforce fine-grained repository permissions and regularly rotate or revoke CI/CD secrets and cloud credentials; additionally, enable GitHub's secret scanning and push-protection features to detect and block credential exposure before workflows execute.
strikes.summary: An attacker leveraged stolen credentials for 4,837 GitHub accounts to inject a secret-stealer payload into repositories those accounts had write access to, targeting CI/CD pipeline secrets and cloud credentials. The malicious workflow ran in at least 1,806 repositories, according to Aikido Security.

strikes.title: ScreenConnect Attacks Target at Least 288 Endpoints Across 48 Organizations With Rogue Clients
strikes.location: Multiple organizations in partner environments using ConnectWise ScreenConnect; ground zero spans at least 48 organizations, specific countries not disclosed.
strikes.data_affected: Endpoints and systems of affected organizations accessed via rogue ScreenConnect remote access clients; scope of data exfiltrated not disclosed.
strikes.impact: At least 288 endpoints across 48 organizations compromised through unauthorized rogue ScreenConnect client deployments; five third-party partner extensions were disabled by ConnectWise as a containment measure.
strikes.prevention: Enforce strict allowlisting and integrity verification of authorized remote access clients, and regularly audit third-party extensions and partner integrations for unauthorized or anomalous activity.
strikes.summary: Attackers deployed rogue ScreenConnect clients to gain unauthorized access to at least 288 endpoints across 48 organizations, prompting ConnectWise to disable five third-party extensions in partner environments as a precautionary measure. ConnectWise stated there is no evidence of a compromise to its own infrastructure or a vulnerability in the ScreenConnect software itself.

strikes.title: AntiFox AI Pentesting Platform Linked to Attacks That Accessed AWS Production Secrets
strikes.location: AWS production cloud environments of victim organizations (specific countries not disclosed); attacker infrastructure hosted on Alibaba Cloud.
strikes.data_affected: AWS production secrets and credentials; internal cloud environment access obtained via lateral movement post-compromise.
strikes.impact: Multiple unnamed organizations had their AWS production credentials stolen and their cloud environments laterally pivoted through; the full scope of affected victims was not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Enforce least-privilege IAM policies and enable AWS CloudTrail with real-time alerting on anomalous credential usage or API calls originating from unexpected sources, to detect and block lateral movement before secrets are exfiltrated.
strikes.summary: An agentic AI penetration-testing platform called AntiFox was used in a campaign to steal AWS production credentials from victim environments. Alibaba Cloud systems hosting AntiFox interfaces were linked to confirmed malicious intrusions that also included lateral movement within compromised environments.

strikes.title: Hackers Target Qlik Sense Servers With Reverse Shells, Stage ActiveMQ and Veeam Exploits
strikes.location: Multiple EU-based customer environments running Qlik Sense servers
strikes.data_affected: Qlik Sense server environments; systems potentially exposed to PowerShell reverse shell execution and ActiveMQ/Veeam exploit staging
strikes.impact: Multiple EU-based organizations were targeted across a narrow timeframe; reverse shell delivery was unsuccessful per the report, but exploit staging activity was confirmed across several customer environments — full operational impact not disclosed
strikes.prevention: Apply all available security patches and hotfixes to Qlik Sense, Apache ActiveMQ, and Veeam installations immediately, and enforce network-level egress filtering to block unauthorized outbound PowerShell connections from analytics and backup servers
strikes.summary: In October 2026, threat actors targeted Qlik Sense servers belonging to multiple EU-based organizations, attempting to deliver PowerShell reverse shell commands within a window of just over three minutes. The campaign, identified by Cynet's CyOps and Research teams, also staged exploits associated with Apache ActiveMQ and Veeam vulnerabilities, though the reverse shell deliveries were reported as unsuccessful.

strikes.title: eMudhra Revokes 8 More CAs It Previously Declared Unaffected by Key Compromise
strikes.location: eMudhra, a licensed Certificate Authority headquartered in India
strikes.data_affected: Private keys and intermediate certificate authority (CA) certificates of 8 additional eMudhra intermediate CAs; at least 8 CAs previously declared unaffected are now revoked.
strikes.impact: eMudhra was forced to revoke 8 more intermediate CAs, expanding the scope of its October key compromise incident. Any digital certificates chaining to these intermediate CAs are invalidated, potentially affecting a broad range of relying parties and certificate subscribers across eMudhra's customer base; exact downstream scale not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Conduct rigorous, isolated code review and automated secrets-scanning of all internal PKI management scripts before deployment, ensuring no single script flaw can touch multiple intermediate CA key-handling routines.
strikes.summary: An in-house Python script used by Indian certificate authority eMudhra was at the centre of an October 2026 private-key compromise; the fallout has now expanded, forcing eMudhra to revoke 8 additional intermediate CAs it had previously declared unaffected. Although the 8 newly revoked intermediate CAs did not have weakened keys, a flaw in a single line of the same script implicated them, requiring full revocation.

strikes.title: Fake Google Update Extension Turns VS Code Into a Malware Delivery Tool
strikes.location: Visual Studio Code users globally; no specific geographic ground zero disclosed — defaulting to Microsoft (VS Code vendor) headquarters, United States.
strikes.data_affected: Developer workstations and systems running Visual Studio Code; potential access to local files, credentials, and code repositories on affected machines.
strikes.impact: Developers who installed the fake extension were exposed to malware delivery through their VS Code environment; the full scope of victims and downstream damage was not disclosed in the report.
strikes.prevention: Strictly vet and allowlist VS Code extensions by publisher identity and install only from verified, official marketplace sources; enforce extension signature verification and use endpoint detection to flag unauthorized extension installations.
strikes.summary: Threat actors distributed a fraudulent "Google Update" browser or VS Code extension that covertly turned Visual Studio Code into a malware delivery platform. The campaign used the trusted VS Code environment as a conduit to deploy malicious payloads on victim machines.

strikes.title: Fandango says hackers stole payment card details from checkout pages
strikes.location: Fandango Media checkout pages — Fandango Media LLC, headquartered in the United States.
strikes.data_affected: Payment card details (card numbers, expiry dates, and potentially other cardholder data) entered by customers on Fandango's checkout pages.
strikes.impact: Fandango Media customers who made purchases through the affected checkout pages had their payment card details exfiltrated; the full scale of affected customers is not disclosed in the report.
strikes.prevention: Implement robust Content Security Policy (CSP) headers and conduct regular integrity monitoring of checkout page scripts to detect and block unauthorized third-party or injected scripts (e.g., web skimmers) in real time.
strikes.summary: Fandango Media suffered a data breach in which hackers injected malicious code into its checkout pages to steal customers' payment card details at the point of entry. The company is actively notifying affected customers about the compromise.

strikes.title: FBI warns ARTEX AI hacking tool is powering global cyberattacks
strikes.location: ConnectWise platform (US-headquartered), affecting Microsoft 365 customer environments globally.
strikes.data_affected: Microsoft 365 customer environments accessed via ConnectWise's platform; full scope of data compromised not disclosed.
strikes.impact: Multiple organizations using ConnectWise-managed Microsoft 365 environments were compromised; exact number of victims not disclosed, but described as global in scale.
strikes.prevention: Enforce least-privilege access and multi-factor authentication on all ConnectWise-managed Microsoft 365 integrations, and monitor for anomalous OAuth or API activity originating from third-party management platforms.
strikes.summary: Hackers leveraging an AI-powered penetration testing framework called ARTEX carried out a supply-chain breach against ConnectWise, compromising Microsoft 365 customer environments worldwide. The FBI issued a warning about ARTEX being used to automate such attacks against organizations globally.

strikes.title: TSMC employee data breach linked to cloud provider
strikes.location: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), Taiwan — breach originated via a third-party cloud provider.
strikes.data_affected: Personal employee data (~6.9 GB), nature of specific fields not disclosed beyond personal information.
strikes.impact: TSMC employees' personal data was exposed and placed up for auction online; the full number of affected individuals and downstream impact were not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Enforce strict third-party vendor security assessments and contractual data-handling obligations for cloud providers, including regular audits and least-privilege access controls to limit exposure of sensitive employee records.
strikes.summary: TSMC confirmed that personal employee data was leaked online after a threat actor listed approximately 6.9 GB of allegedly stolen company data for auction. The breach was linked to a third-party cloud provider rather than TSMC's own internal systems.

strikes.title: Cursor confirms security breach led to malicious Claude Code extension
strikes.location: Cursor's extension marketplace (Cursor, Inc. — US-based AI code editor) and Fireworks AI infrastructure (US-based AI platform provider).
strikes.data_affected: Credentials belonging to Fireworks AI; Cursor's extension marketplace integrity; users' development environments potentially exposed via the malicious Claude Code extension.
strikes.impact: Cursor IDE users who installed the malicious Claude Code extension from the marketplace were put at risk of compromise. The breach undermined trust in Cursor's extension ecosystem; full scope of affected users not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Implement cryptographic code-signing and rigorous integrity verification for all marketplace extensions, ensuring any tampered or newly published package is flagged and quarantined before it reaches end-users.
strikes.summary: Cursor confirmed a security breach in which attackers stole credentials from AI infrastructure provider Fireworks AI and used them to distribute a malicious Claude Code extension through Cursor's marketplace. The compromised extension exposed users of the Cursor IDE to potential downstream compromise via the tampered plugin.

strikes.title: Trezor confirms crypto-stealing implants in three wallets, releases fix
strikes.location: Southeast Asia — via reseller CryptoBilis, affecting end customers of Trezor Safe 5 wallets
strikes.data_affected: Wallet recovery phrases (seed phrases) stored on Trezor Safe 5 hardware wallets
strikes.impact: At least three Trezor Safe 5 devices sold through reseller CryptoBilis were compromised; buyers of those devices faced direct risk of full cryptocurrency wallet takeover. Scale of financial losses to end users not disclosed.
strikes.prevention: Purchase hardware wallets exclusively from the manufacturer's official store or verified direct-sales channels, and perform firmware/hardware integrity verification upon receipt before initializing any wallet.
strikes.summary: Trezor confirmed that three Safe 5 hardware wallets sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis contained malicious hardware implants designed to steal wallet recovery phrases. The implants exfiltrated the stolen phrases to attackers via cellular networks, posing a direct threat to victims' cryptocurrency holdings.

strikes.title: German military drone operations disrupted by cyberattack
strikes.location: Quantum Systems, a German defense technology company (headquarters: Germany)
strikes.data_affected: Drone operations systems and defense technology infrastructure at Quantum Systems; specific data or systems compromised not fully disclosed.
strikes.impact: German military drone operations were disrupted; the full operational and strategic scope of the fallout was not disclosed in the report.
strikes.prevention: Implement network segmentation and air-gapping of operational technology systems supporting military drone command-and-control infrastructure to limit attacker lateral movement and disruptive reach.
strikes.summary: German defense technology company Quantum Systems confirmed it detected a cyberattack by "hostile actors" in late October 2026 that disrupted military drone operations. The company characterized the incident as an active cyberattack rather than an opportunistic or accidental event.
